title: Afghanistan: 5 Years in the Dark
author: Nasratullah Taban
text:
Credit: X/UN Women Afghanistan
Fatima keeps her medical textbooks in a cupboard she no longer opens. Her university ID card, with its photograph of a 19-year-old who intended to become a doctor, sits among them like a relic from another country. In a sense, it is. The Afghanistan that printed the card – a state with a constitution, a free press and women in its universities, courtrooms, and newsrooms – no longer exists.“Sometimes I look at a bird and feel jealous, because it has more freedom than I do,” she told me from Kabul, where, at 24, she describes herself as a prisoner in her own home. “I often think that if the Taliban had not come, I would still be at university, working toward my biggest dream of becoming a doctor. Now, instead of dreaming about my future, I spend my days wondering how I will survive and asking myself, ‘Why me?’”[...]
